defect: S18 prescribes a remedy it never teaches. S18-T3-A instructs the learner to 'Lista causas comunes y diseños que las romperían (experimento, instrumento) antes de cualquier afirmación causal'. S18-T2-B builds an A-versus-B comparison (mean 94 vs 108, Cohen's d 1.118) and closes with 'no veredicto causal de campaña'. selfCheck Q8 quizzes that same comparison. youDo requires 'Interpretar correlación/Spearman o segmentos sin afirmaciones causales'. Nowhere in the 52 active sections is a randomised experiment defined.
evidence: grep 'aleatoriz' across all 52 active section files: zero hits
grep 'randomiz' / 'grupo de control': hits only in s09-sklearn.ts, which index.ts does not import
grep 'estimand', 'guardrail', 'peeking', 'multiple testing', 'significancia practica': zero hits in active files
body read of S18-T2-B lines 150-201 and S18-T3-A lines 202-250
learner_consequence: The learner is told four times that causal language requires a design they are never taught. They leave S18 holding a prohibition with no route past it, and cannot act on the section's own instruction. Writing protocol 3.3 forbids exactly this ('assumes hidden knowledge', 'introduces terminology without clarifying it').
acceptance: A learner finishing S18 can name unit/treatment/control/outcome/estimand, explain what random assignment buys and does not buy, read an effect with its interval, refuse both standard p-value misreadings, distinguish statistical from practical significance, name a primary metric and a guardrail, and explain why peeking and multiple testing inflate false positives.

defect: S15-T4-A teaches Parquet purely as a type-preservation device ('preserva tipos de forma nativa'), with round-trip, index=False and the Unnamed:0 trap. Nothing in the 52 active sections explains why a columnar layout lets a reader skip work. The learner is asked to choose a storage format without any model of what the choice costs or saves.

learner_consequence: Format choice stays a ritual. The learner cannot reason about why three columns out of forty are cheap to read, cannot predict when partitioning will help, and cannot recognise the small-files trade-off later in S46.
acceptance: The learner can explain row versus column physical layout, projection pushdown, row-group statistics and pruning, and can state the two limits (useless statistics when data is unsorted; small-file overhead when over-partitioned).
